description: TEST FIXTURE for safe_expressions regex allowlists (R3). Exact lists EMPTY; only the *_regex keys are populated, proving regex-only operation.
_comment_safe_expressions: Broad-patterns + static denylist fixture (2026-09-19 design). The ONE exact allow entry below is a deliberate trap: it must still be DENIED by the bare-name deny entry (precedence proof, case D1). dotnet_method_allowlist would default to the built-in ~40-name list, so the instance positive case uses ToCharArray which is NOT in that default.

safe_expressions._comment_exact_trap: Deliberately exact-allowed AND denylisted: proves deny-exact outranks exact-allow + Class-A row + get family (case D1).
safe_expressions._comment_static_regex: Broad-patterns rows per design 2026-09-19 section 4. Every row anchored ^...$ (D1). Case-insensitive.
safe_expressions._comment_denylist: STATIC denylist (NEW, 2026-09-19): checked FIRST in Test-SafeAst, outranks every allow path. Exact entries may be Type::Method or bare Method (any type). 'intern' pins Q4: string::Intern stays ask despite the whole-type string row.
safe_expressions._comment_denylist_regex: TAIL-anchored so they catch BOTH reflected full names AND non-canonical written spellings (alias forms with no reflected key). Leading segment is OPTIONAL ([\w.]* not \w[\w.]*) so a bare [Marshal] / [IsolatedStorageFile] spelling (written key only, no reflected key) is still denied - TDD fix 2026-09-19.
safe_expressions._comment_instance_regex: ToCharArray is deliberately NOT in the built-in default instance list, so an allow can only come from this regex (proves regex-only operation).
